name: Rava Dosa
cuisine: South Indian (Karnataka/Tamil Nadu Udupi-hotel classic; a staple of Mumbai's Udupi restaurants)

ingredients.name: Semolina (rava / sooji), fine or medium (Bombay rava)
Water
ingredients.householdMeasure: about ¾ cup + 2 tbsp (added in parts)

ingredients.name: Onion, finely chopped
ingredients.householdMeasure: ½ small onion (about ⅓ cup chopped)

equipment: Flat tawa (dosa pan), at least 25 cm wide
Mixing bowl (medium; the batter is watery, so leave room to whisk)
Whisk or a spoon/fork for mixing
Ladle or a small steel cup (katori, about 100 ml) for pouring; no ladle → pour from a small steel glass
Flat metal or silicone spatula (turner) for lifting and folding
Chopping board and knife (for onion, chilli, ginger, curry leaves, coriander)
Measuring spoons and a measuring cup; no set → a normal tablespoon/teaspoon and a 200 ml steel glass (about ¾ cup + 2 tbsp of water ≈ 1 glass)
Half an onion or a paper towel to grease/wipe the tawa (traditional trick: rub the cut onion dipped in oil over the hot cast-iron tawa)
Small bowl of water and a wet cloth (to sprinkle and wipe the tawa between dosas, cast iron only)

steps.title: Measure the flours
steps.text: Put 25 g (2½ tbsp) rava, 25 g (3 tbsp) rice flour and 10 g (1 heaped tbsp) maida in the mixing bowl.
steps.visualCue: Three small heaps: cream rava, white rice flour, white maida
steps.cameraCheck: The bowl with the three flours
steps.videoShot: Spoons of each flour going into the bowl.

steps.title: Add the dry spices
steps.text: Add ¼ tsp salt, ¼ tsp cumin seeds and ¼ tsp coarsely crushed black pepper.
steps.visualCue: Brown cumin and black pepper bits on top of the flour
steps.cameraCheck: The bowl from above
steps.videoShot: Crushed pepper sprinkled over the flour.

steps.title: Mix the dry ingredients
steps.text: Stir with a spoon so the flours and spices are evenly blended.
steps.visualCue: One even, pale mixture with spice specks spread through
steps.cameraCheck: The mixed flour
steps.videoShot: Spoon turning the flour.

steps.title: Add the curd and the first water
steps.text: Add 1 tbsp (15 g) curd and 120 ml (½ cup) water.
steps.visualCue: A thick, lumpy paste
steps.cameraCheck: The bowl with curd and water added
steps.videoShot: Water poured in over the curd.

steps.title: Whisk until smooth
steps.text: Whisk well, pressing out any lumps against the side of the bowl.
steps.tip: Get rid of lumps now, while the batter is thick; it is much harder once it is watery.
steps.visualCue: No dry lumps; a smooth, thick-ish batter like pancake batter
steps.cameraCheck: The batter dripping off the whisk
steps.videoShot: The whisk lifting smooth batter.

steps.title: Thin the batter
steps.text: Add another 70 ml (about 5 tbsp) water and whisk again.
steps.tip: This is the most important rule. A thick batter makes a soft, heavy dosa with no lacy holes.
steps.visualCue: Very thin and watery, like buttermilk (chaas); it runs off the spoon in a thin stream, not in blobs
steps.cameraCheck: The batter poured from a spoon
steps.videoShot: Batter running off the ladle in a thin stream.

steps.title: Chop the onion
steps.text: Finely chop 40 g (½ small) onion. Keep it aside in a small bowl.
steps.visualCue: Small, even pieces about the size of a rice grain
steps.cameraCheck: ⅓ cup chopped onion in a bowl
steps.videoShot: Knife chopping onion finely.

steps.title: Chop the aromatics
steps.text: Finely chop 1 small green chilli, ½ inch ginger, 6–8 curry leaves and 1 tbsp coriander leaves.
steps.visualCue: Four small green-and-yellow heaps on the board
steps.cameraCheck: The chopped chilli, ginger, curry leaves and coriander
steps.videoShot: Knife running through curry leaves.

steps.title: Add the aromatics to the batter
steps.text: Stir the chilli, ginger, curry leaves and coriander into the batter. (Keep the onion separate for the tawa.)
steps.visualCue: Green flecks spread through the thin batter
steps.cameraCheck: The batter with greens
steps.videoShot: Herbs stirred into the batter.

steps.title: Rest the batter
steps.text: Leave the bowl uncovered on the counter.
steps.tip: The rava soaks up water while resting, so the batter thickens a little. No fermentation is needed.
steps.visualCue: The rava has settled at the bottom and the top looks watery
steps.cameraCheck: The resting batter
steps.videoShot: The bowl sitting next to a timer.

steps.title: Check and adjust the batter
steps.text: Stir from the bottom. If it has thickened, add 1–2 tbsp more water (up to about 210 ml in total).
steps.visualCue: Back to a thin, buttermilk-like flow
steps.cameraCheck: Batter flowing off the ladle
steps.videoShot: Ladle lifting and dropping thin batter.

steps.title: Heat the tawa
steps.text: Put the tawa on medium-high heat.
steps.visualCue: A few drops of water sprinkled on it sizzle and vanish within 2–3 seconds
steps.cameraCheck: Water drops sizzling on the tawa
steps.videoShot: Water flicked onto the hot tawa, hissing.

steps.title: Season the tawa
steps.text: Rub a few drops of oil over the tawa with a cut onion half or paper towel. (Cast iron: then sprinkle a little water and wipe it off with a wet cloth to cool the surface slightly.)
steps.tip: On a non-stick tawa, just a few drops of oil wiped with a paper towel is enough.
steps.visualCue: A thin, even sheen; no pools of oil
steps.cameraCheck: The shiny tawa
steps.videoShot: Onion half rubbing oil across the tawa.

steps.title: Sprinkle the onion
steps.text: Scatter half the chopped onion (20 g) over the centre of the tawa in a rough circle.
steps.visualCue: Onion bits spread over an area about 20 cm wide
steps.cameraCheck: Onion on the tawa
steps.videoShot: Hand scattering onion over the tawa.

steps.title: Stir the batter
steps.text: Stir the batter well from the bottom right before pouring.
steps.tip: Skip this and your first dosa will be all water and your last one all rava.
steps.visualCue: The settled rava is lifted back into the batter
steps.cameraCheck: The ladle scraping the bottom of the bowl
steps.videoShot: Ladle stirring from the bottom.

steps.title: Pour the dosa
steps.text: Take about half the batter (one ladle, about 120 ml). From about 15 cm above the tawa, pour it in a thin stream, starting at the outer edge and moving in circles towards the centre. Fill only large gaps; small holes are what you want. Do not spread it with the ladle.
steps.tip: Pouring from the outside in gives a crisp, even edge. If the batter does not sizzle, the tawa is not hot enough.
steps.visualCue: A lacy, net-like circle with many small holes that sizzles immediately
steps.cameraCheck: The freshly poured dosa
steps.videoShot: Batter streaming from a height into a lacy circle.

steps.title: Add the oil
steps.text: Drizzle 1 tsp (5 ml) oil around the edge and over the holes.
steps.visualCue: Oil bubbling in the holes and at the edges
steps.cameraCheck: The oil drizzle on the dosa
steps.videoShot: Oil dropped from a spoon around the dosa.

steps.title: Cook until crisp
steps.text: Cook on medium-high without touching it.
steps.tip: Rava dosa takes longer than a normal dosa. If you lift it early, it tears. Flipping is optional; most hotels don't.
steps.visualCue: The top looks dry and set, the base is golden-brown, and the edges lift away from the tawa on their own
steps.cameraCheck: The lifted golden edge
steps.videoShot: Edge curling up from the tawa.

steps.title: Fold and remove
steps.text: Slide the spatula under the dosa, fold it in half (or roll it), and lift it onto a plate.
steps.visualCue: A crisp, golden, lacy dosa that holds its shape
steps.cameraCheck: The folded dosa on the plate
steps.videoShot: Spatula folding and lifting the dosa.

steps.title: Reset the tawa
steps.text: Reduce the heat for 20 seconds. (Cast iron: sprinkle water and wipe.) Then turn it back to medium-high.
steps.visualCue: The tawa is clean, with no burnt bits; water sizzles again before you pour
steps.cameraCheck: The clean tawa
steps.videoShot: Wet cloth wiping the tawa.

steps.title: Make the second dosa
steps.text: Repeat steps 14 to 19 with the remaining onion, batter (stir first) and 1 tsp oil.
steps.visualCue: Same golden, lacy dosa
steps.cameraCheck: Two dosas on the plate
steps.videoShot: The second lacy dosa crisping.

steps.title: Serve at once
steps.text: Serve hot with coconut chutney and/or sambar.
steps.visualCue: Crisp dosas that crackle when you tear them
steps.cameraCheck: The plate with dosas and sides
steps.videoShot: Hand tearing a crackling piece of dosa.

researchRating.basis: rava dosa is one of the most-ordered and most-praised Udupi dishes, regularly named in Mumbai "best dosa" guides (e.g. Mysore onion rava sada at Hotel Ramashray, Matunga; rava dosa at Cafe Madras and Mani's) and very popular on Indian recipe blogs as an instant, no-fermentation dosa. Points are lost for common home complaints in recipe comments and FAQs: dosas sticking, breaking or turning soft when the batter is too thick or the tawa too cool, and that it is harder to master than it looks.

storage: Cooked dosas are best not stored: they turn soft and leathery. If you must, refrigerate in a closed box for up to 1 day and reheat on a hot tawa for 1 minute per side (they crisp up a little). Not suitable for the freezer. Leftover batter: fridge, covered, up to 1 day (the curd and onion-free greens keep fine; add onion only on the tawa). Stir well and add 2–4 tbsp water before using, because the rava keeps absorbing water.
leftoverRemix: Rava dosa kothu. Tear 1–2 leftover dosas into small pieces. Fry ½ chopped onion, ½ chopped tomato and a pinch of chilli powder and garam masala in 1 tsp oil, add the dosa pieces and 2 tbsp leftover sambar or salan, and toss on high heat for 2 minutes until coated and lightly crisp at the edges. Top with coriander and a squeeze of lemon. It turns soggy dosas into a spicy, street-style stir-fry, like kothu parotta.
burnOff: about 4.7 km of running (330 ÷ 70 kcal/km, 70 kg adult), or about 6.6 km of brisk walking (about 80 minutes at 5 km/h, at about 50 kcal/km) (est.). With sambar and chutney (about 500 kcal): about 7.1 km running or 10 km walking (est.).

navratri.reason: the batter is semolina (wheat), rice flour and maida, and grains are not eaten on the common vrat rule set; a vrat dosa would be a different dish (e.g. samak rice or kuttu flour), not rava dosa

ekadashi.reason: contains rice flour and wheat (rava, maida), and grains, especially rice, are avoided on Ekadashi

jain.reason: skip the onion and fresh ginger (root vegetables) and use a pinch of dry ginger powder (sonth) or just green chilli, pepper and cumin; Mumbai menus already sell "Jain Rava Dosa" (e.g. Ayyappan Idli Stall, BKC on Zomato; Idli Dosa Fusion, Malad on magicpin)

ramadan.reason: vegetarian with no meat (no halal concern) and light; it is mostly refined carbohydrate, so pair it with sambar (protein from dal) for sehri to stay full longer
